SMTO-CFG-0038 — SMTO's settings file doesn't start with named settings

GUID: 71943ceb-48f1-441b-a46d-9ac43fa85302
Slug: config-invalid-app-config-yaml-at-expected-a
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO read its startup settings file (usually config.yaml), but instead of named sections such as llm: and runtime:, it found a list or a single value at the top, so it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file named in the message in a plain text editor. The problem is in how the file begins, so you need to see its first lines.
  2. Make each top-level line a section name with a colon, such as llm:, server: or runtime:, with its settings indented below. Remove any leading dash (-) or lone word. SMTO expects named sections at the top; a leading dash turns the whole file into a list it can't use.
  3. If you're unsure what the file should contain, put back the last copy that worked, then start SMTO again. A known-good copy lets SMTO start while the change is checked separately.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message and send it with the file, after removing any passwords or API keys, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep starting SMTO with the same file; it is refused the same way every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration loading failed because the selected application YAML parsed to a top-level value that is not a mapping (for example a list or a single scalar).

What this means

  • Parsed nonempty YAML is not a top-level mapping; empty/falsy input is normalized to an empty mapping before this check. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Parsed nonempty YAML is not a top-level mapping; empty/falsy input is normalized to an empty mapping before this check.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the top-level parsed shape separately from YAML syntax and nested field validation.

How to fix it

  • The selected file parsed as YAML but its root is a list or scalar rather than a mapping (an empty file is treated as an empty mapping). Restructure it as a top-level mapping with keys such as config_version, server, llm, runtime and sql, and validate it with aor doctor --config before restarting.
  • Correct the YAML syntax and use a top-level mapping in the application configuration. Keep private values in their supported configuration fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The file yields a mapping of supported application configuration sections.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
